question: What do the different columns in the stock moves history report show, like the reference and status fields?
answer: The Moves History report's columns represent: Date (calendar date and time of the stock move); Reference (description of the reason for the stock move or quantity change, such as a receipt number like WH/IN/00012); Product (name of the product involved in the move); Lot/Serial Number (the lot or serial number of the tracked product being moved); From (source location of the moved product); To (destination location of the moved product); Quantity (number of products moved); Unit (unit of measure of the products moved); and Status (indicates the move status, which can be Done, quantities to complete the operation) [1].

question: How can I make Odoo pick the smallest number of packages when fulfilling an order for a product?
answer: Enable the Packages feature, then set the product category's Force Removal Strategy to Least Packages. With this strategy, Odoo fulfills an order by opening the fewest number of packages [1][2]. For example, if a 100 kg package has been opened and depleted to 54 kg, an order for 14 kg picks from that opened package; an order exceeding 54 kg uses an unopened 100 kg package, and the open packages are prioritized in the next picking [1]. To verify where units were picked, on the delivery order select the bulleted list icon to open the Open: Stock move pop-up, where the Pick from field shows the source [2].
reason: The answer correctly states the key steps (enable Packages, set Force Removal Strategy to Least Packages) and describes the least-packages behavior, with extra detail that does not contradict the reference.

question: What do the international trade terms like EXW or CIF mean, and which ones are available in Odoo?
answer: Incoterms (International Commercial Terms) are standardized trade terms used in international transactions to define the rights and responsibilities of buyers and sellers, establishing obligations related to delivery of goods, transfer of risks, and distribution of costs between the parties [1]. By default, all 11 Incoterms are available in Odoo: EXW (Ex works), FCA (Free carrier), FAS (Free alongside ship), FOB (Free on board), CFR (Cost and freight), CIF (Cost, insurance and freight), CPT (Carriage paid to), CIP (Carriage and insurance paid to), DPU (Delivered at place unloaded), DAP (Delivered at place), and DDP (Delivered duty paid) [1].
reason: The answer defines Incoterms and lists all 11 available in Odoo, matching the reference.

question: When does Odoo automatically recalculate taxes on a quote or invoice?

question: How do I set up a new direct debit mandate for a customer so I can collect payments from them?
answer: To create a new direct debit mandate, open the Accounting app and go to Customers > Direct Debit Mandates, then click New [1]. Fill out the Customer (the customer whose payments will be managed by this mandate), the IBAN (the customer's account to collect payments from), the SDD Scheme (select CORE for B2C customers and B2B for B2B customers), and optionally an End Date after which the mandate closes automatically; if left empty, the mandate remains active until closed or revoked [1]. Note that a valid IBAN must be defined in the bank journal used to receive SDD payments for the mandate, and the B2B scheme is optional and offered exclusively to business payers—some banks or businesses might not accept B2B SDD [1]. Then click Send & Print to generate a PDF of the mandate form and send it to the customer for signature, and click Validate to activate the mandate [1]. To print the mandate form after validation, click the gear icon and select Mandate form [1]. Before this, SDD must be enabled: go to Accounting > Configuration > Settings, scroll to the Customer Payments section, enable SEPA Direct Debit (SDD), and click Save; then set the company's Creditor Identifier and click Save [2].

question: How do I scrap a product while I'm processing a receipt or delivery order in Odoo?
answer: To scrap a product during an operation such as a receipt or delivery order, navigate to the Inventory app. From the Inventory Overview, click the # To Process button on the operation's task card (e.g., the Receipts task card). Select an operation to process from the resulting list of existing orders to open that operation's form. Click the cog (fa-cog) icon and select Scrap from the drop-down menu, which opens a Scrap Products pop-up window. In the pop-up, select the products from the operation to be scrapped from the Product drop-down, and adjust the Quantity if necessary. If the product is tracked by lot or serial number, a Lot/Serial field appears where you specify the tracking number. The Source Location and Scrap Location can be changed if needed, and if a replenishment rule is set up and the product should be replenished, tick the Replenish Quantities checkbox. Click Scrap Products to finish. A Scraps smart button then appears at the top of the operation form; click it to view details of all scrap orders created from that operation.
reason: The answer includes all key steps from the reference (Inventory app, # To Process, cog icon, Scrap, pop-up product/quantity/lot-serial, Scrap Products, Scraps smart button) and adds consistent extra detail without contradicting it.

question: How do I move last year's profits into an equity account and then lock the books so nobody can change them?
answer: To allocate the current year's earnings, create a new miscellaneous entry with a date set to the end of the fiscal year to book them to any equity account [1]. Then verify that the current year's earnings on the balance sheet correctly show a zero balance; if so, a Hard Lock date can be set to the last day of the fiscal year in Accounting > Accounting > Lock Dates [1]. Note that the Hard Lock date field is irreversible and cannot be changed or overridden regardless of access rights, so it should only be set once confirmed correct [1]. Alternatively, to prevent modifications to posted journal entries on or before a date, set a Lock Everything date by going to Accounting > Accounting > Lock Dates, and in the Lock Journal Entries window set the Lock Everything date and Save [2].

question: How can I make Odoo reserve stock a few days ahead of the scheduled delivery date instead of right at it?

Once selected, a new 'Reserve before scheduled date' field appears below, where you can change the 'days before' value (default 0) to set the maximum number of days before a scheduled date that products should be reserved; the 'days before when starred' value sets this for starred (favorited) transfers [3]. For example, with days before set to 2 and days before when starred set to 3, products are reserved two days before the scheduled delivery date for normal orders and three days before for starred transfers [3].

question: How can I set up a product so that Odoo only orders or produces it after a customer actually places an order, instead of keeping stock on hand?
answer: Use the Make to Order replenishment strategy: procurement or production is triggered only after a sales order is confirmed, and Odoo automatically links the sales order to the generated order/route. It is the best strategy for customized products and/or products with no stock kept on-hand. [1]

question: How do I renumber a batch of vendor bills so they follow a continuous sequence after importing them from my old accounting system?

question: How do I set up a rule so that a specific product gets automatically stored in a particular sub-location when it arrives in my warehouse?
answer: First, activate the Multi-Step Routes feature under Inventory app > Configuration > Settings (this also automatically activates Storage Locations), then click Save [1]. To define the rule, navigate to Inventory app > Configuration > Putaway Rules and click New to configure a new putaway rule on a Product or Product Category [1]. In the 'When product arrives in location' field, set the location where the rule is triggered (e.g., WH/Stock), and in the 'Store to' field set the destination sub-location (e.g., WH/Stock/Fruits) [1]. The Store to location must be a sub-location of the first location [1]. For example, to store all apples in the fruits section, fill the Store to field with WH/Stock/Fruits when the Product, Apple, arrives in WH/Stock, then hit Save [1]. Use the Sublocation field to specify whether to use a sublocation or a storage category: 'No' means no sublocation is used; 'Last Used' uses the last location that had a move associated with it for that product; 'Closest Location' uses the locations specified as part of a storage category, which is mandatory in the Having Category field [1].
